# Acronyms and Technical Glossary {#sec-appendix-d-glossary}

::: {.abstract}
This reference appendix consolidates and categorizes the technical acronyms, standards, formal representations, and abbreviations used throughout *Architecture 2.0*. Each entry lists the canonical abbreviation, its spelled-out form per the *Chicago Manual of Style*, and a concise engineering definition, grouped by technical domain across hardware microarchitecture (@tbl-glossary-hardware), physical design and signoff (@tbl-glossary-physical), EDA and compilers (@tbl-glossary-compilers), verification and standards (@tbl-glossary-verification), bus interconnects (@tbl-glossary-interconnects), and AI automation (@tbl-glossary-ai).
:::

## Hardware Architecture and Microarchitecture {#sec-glossary-hardware}

| **Acronym** | **Spelled-out form** | **Engineering definition** |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **ABI** | application binary interface | The low-level binary interface between software programs and the operating system or hardware register state. |
| **AMX** | Advanced Matrix Extensions | A proprietary matrix acceleration instruction set extension developed by Intel for high-throughput tensor arithmetic. |
| **ASIC** | application-specific integrated circuit | A custom-manufactured integrated circuit tailored to execute a specific computing workload with maximal energy and area efficiency. |
| **CPU** | central processing unit | The primary general-purpose execution engine that sequences and executes instruction streams in a computer system. |
| **DDR** | double data rate | A memory bus protocol that transfers data on both the rising and falling edges of the clock cycle. |
| **DMA** | direct memory access | A hardware feature allowing peripheral devices or accelerators to transfer data directly to and from main memory without processor intervention. |
| **DSA** | domain-specific architecture | A customized processor or compute engine engineered specifically to maximize execution efficiency for a targeted family of workloads. |
| **DVFS** | dynamic voltage and frequency scaling | A power management technique that dynamically adjusts operating voltage and clock frequency to balance performance against thermal dissipation. |
| **FIFO** | first-in, first-out | A queue data structure or buffer hardware where the earliest stored data elements are retrieved first. |
| **FPGA** | field-programmable gate array | A reconfigurable integrated circuit containing programmable logic blocks and routing channels configured post-fabrication. |
| **GDDR5** | Graphics Double Data Rate 5 | A high-bandwidth synchronous graphics random-access memory interface standard tailored for parallel data-intensive computing. |
| **GEMM** | general matrix multiply | The canonical linear algebra compute kernel forming the computational core of deep neural network acceleration. |
| **GPU** | graphics processing unit | A massively parallel processor optimized for high-throughput rasterization, linear algebra, and tensor operations. |
| **HBM** | High Bandwidth Memory | A high-speed 3D-stacked DRAM memory architecture providing massive memory bandwidth through wide through-silicon via (TSV) interconnects. |
| **HDL** | hardware description language | A specialized formal language (such as SystemVerilog or VHDL) used to model the structure, behavior, and timing of digital electronic circuits. |
| **HPC** | high-performance computing | The practice of aggregating computing power to perform complex calculations at massively parallel scales. |
| **IPC** | instructions per cycle | A standard microarchitectural throughput metric measuring the average number of instructions executed per clock cycle. |
| **ISA** | instruction set architecture | The abstract model and boundary defining instructions, registers, addressing modes, and memory consistency for a processor. |
| **KGD** | known-good die | A bare semiconductor die or chiplet that has been comprehensively tested and verified to meet functional and electrical specifications prior to multi-die package assembly. |
| **MSHR** | miss status holding register | A specialized hardware buffer in non-blocking caches tracking in-flight memory requests to allow cache lookups to continue during outstanding misses. |
| **NoC** | network-on-chip | An on-die packet-switched communication subsystem connecting processing elements, caches, and memory controllers. |
| **NPU** | neural processing unit | A specialized hardware accelerator designed specifically for accelerating tensor operations and deep neural network workloads. |
| **NUMA** | non-uniform memory access | A multiprocessing system architecture where memory access latency varies depending on the physical proximity of the memory module to the requesting processor core. |
| **PE** | processing element | An individual arithmetic compute node or execution unit within a systolic array or parallel accelerator matrix. |
| **RISC** | reduced instruction set computer | A processor design philosophy based on simplified instructions that execute in a single cycle with load-store memory access. |
| **ROB** | reorder buffer | A circular FIFO buffer in out-of-order execution processors tracking in-flight speculative instructions to ensure in-order retirement and precise exceptions. |
| **RTL** | register-transfer level | A digital design modeling abstraction describing synchronous signal and data transfers between hardware registers through combinational logic. |
| **SIMD** | single instruction, multiple data | An execution model in which one instruction applies the same operation to many data elements in parallel across a wide vector register. |
| **SoC** | system-on-chip | An integrated circuit consolidating an entire electronic or computing system onto a single semiconductor die. |
| **SPMD** | single-program, multiple-data | A parallel programming model in which every thread runs the same program over a distinct slice of the data, indexed by its own thread identifier. |
| **SRAM** | static random-access memory | Fast, volatile semiconductor memory using bistable latching circuitry used for on-chip caches and scratchpads. |
| **TCM** | tightly coupled memory | Fast, deterministic on-chip static RAM mapped directly into the processor core's memory map with zero wait states. |
| **TDP** | thermal design power | The maximum sustained power consumption that a cooling system is engineered to dissipate under worst-case operational workloads. |
| **TLB** | translation lookaside buffer | A dedicated hardware cache that stores recent virtual-to-physical address translations to accelerate memory access. |
| **TPU** | Tensor Processing Unit | A custom-developed application-specific integrated circuit engineered by Google specifically for accelerating machine learning training and inference workloads. |
| **TSO** | Total Store Order | A hardware memory consistency model guaranteeing that store operations from a given thread appear in program order to all processors. |
| **WSC** | warehouse-scale computing | Massive datacenter computing systems engineered as a unified, coordinated warehouse of compute nodes, storage, and networking. |
: **Hardware Architecture and Microarchitecture Glossary.** {#tbl-glossary-hardware tbl-colwidths="[15,30,55]"}

## Physical Design, Manufacturing and Signoff {#sec-glossary-physical}

| **Acronym** | **Spelled-out form** | **Engineering definition** |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **BSPDN** | backside power delivery network | A 3D semiconductor manufacturing technology that moves the power distribution metal grid to the backside of the silicon wafer to reduce IR-drop and routing congestion. |
| **DEF** | Design Exchange Format | An open ASCII representation format for transferring physical layout, placement, and routing data between EDA physical design tools. |
| **DRC** | design rule check | Automated verification checking that a physical IC layout complies with the geometric constraints dictated by the semiconductor foundry's manufacturing process. |
| **ECO** | engineering change order | A formal modification process applied late in the design or physical layout cycle to fix bugs or timing violations with minimal disruption to the netlist. |
| **ESD** | electrostatic discharge | A sudden transient flow of electric current between charged bodies that requires on-chip protection structures to prevent physical dielectric breakdown. |
| **EVM** | emergency voltage mitigation | Dynamic hardware circuitry that rapidly detects supply voltage droop and temporarily throttles clock frequency or compute activity. |
| **GAAFET** | gate-all-around field-effect transistor | An advanced transistor architecture where the gate material surrounds all sides of vertically stacked nanosheet or nanowire conduction channels. |
| **GDSII** | Graphic Database System II | The industry-standard binary format for representing integrated circuit planar geometric layout artwork transferred to foundries for photomask fabrication. |
| **IR-drop** | voltage drop | The parasitic reduction in supply voltage across a power distribution network caused by current flow through resistive on-chip metal tracks. |
| **LEF** | Library Exchange Format | An ASCII data format describing standard cell and macro pin geometries, routing layers, and obstruction boundaries for automated place-and-route tools. |
| **LP** | low-power | A foundry process node or silicon design methodology optimized for minimal active switching and subthreshold leakage power. |
| **LVS** | layout versus schematic | Verification confirming that drawn physical layout mask geometry matches the electrical connectivity of the synthesized netlist. |
| **MPW** | multi-project wafer | A shared semiconductor fabrication shuttle run combining multiple distinct customer designs onto common reticle masks to amortize tooling charges. |
| **MTBF** | mean time between failures | The predicted elapsed time between inherent operational failures of a hardware system during normal operation. |
| **NDA** | nondisclosure agreement | A confidential legal contract protecting proprietary process design kits, standard cell libraries, and foundry yield data from unauthorized disclosure. |
| **NRE** | non-recurring engineering | The one-time, upfront engineering and mask tooling costs required to design, verify, and fabricate a new chip design before mass production. |
| **PDK** | process design kit | A collection of device models, design rules, standard-cell libraries, and verification decks supplied by a foundry for a specific fabrication process. |
| **PDN** | power delivery network | The on-die, package, and board-level metal interconnect network distributing supply voltage and ground across all active circuitry. |
| **PVT** | process, voltage, and temperature | The three primary operational variation axes evaluated during static timing and power signoff across fast/slow silicon corners. |
| **SEU** | single-event upset | A soft error or radiation-induced state change in a microelectronic device caused by ionizing radiation. |
| **SNM** | static noise margin | A circuit figure of merit measuring the maximum DC noise voltage an SRAM bitcell can tolerate without inadvertently flipping its stored logic state. |
| **STA** | static timing analysis | A deterministic verification method calculating circuit delays across all signal paths to verify setup and hold timing without dynamic simulation. |
| **TCO** | total cost of ownership | A financial estimate encompassing all direct and indirect capital expenditures and operational costs over the lifetime of a computing system. |
| **TNS** | Total Negative Slack | The cumulative sum of all negative timing slacks across all violating endpoints in a design's static timing analysis graph. |
| **VLSI** | very-large-scale integration | The process of creating integrated circuits by combining millions or billions of MOS transistors onto a single silicon chip. |
: **Physical Design, Manufacturing and Signoff Glossary.** {#tbl-glossary-physical tbl-colwidths="[15,30,55]"}

## EDA, Compilers and Intermediate Representations {#sec-glossary-compilers}

| **Acronym** | **Spelled-out form** | **Engineering definition** |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **AIG** | and-inverter graph | A directed acyclic graph representation of a combinational logic circuit composed entirely of two-input AND nodes and logical inverters. |
| **AST** | abstract syntax tree | A tree representation of the abstract syntactic structure of source code, capturing grammatical hierarchy without formatting tokens. |
| **CAD** | computer-aided design | Software tools used by engineers to create, modify, analyze, and optimize physical hardware and circuit designs. |
| **CDFG** | control-data flow graph | A directed graph representation capturing both control branches and data dependencies within a computational block. |
| **CIRCT** | Circuit IR Compilers and Tools | An open-source, LLVM/MLIR-based hardware compiler infrastructure providing dialect-driven lowering from high-level abstractions to synthesizable RTL. |
| **EDA** | electronic design automation | The category of software tools, algorithms, and workflows used to design, simulate, verify, and physically layout electronic systems and semiconductors. |
| **FIRRTL** | Flexible Intermediate Representation for RTL | An intermediate representation designed for hardware digital design and compiler passes in the Chisel and CIRCT ecosystems. |
| **FSDB** | Fast Signal Database | A high-performance proprietary binary waveform database format widely used for storing simulation and emulation signal traces. |
| **HLS** | high-level synthesis | An automated compilation process transforming algorithmic descriptions into cycle-accurate register-transfer level hardware. |
| **IR** | intermediate representation | A standardized internal data structure or code format used by compilers to represent program or hardware semantics between passes. |
| **JIT** | just-in-time | A compilation strategy where intermediate representations or bytecode are compiled into native machine code dynamically during program execution. |
| **MLIR** | Multi-Level Intermediate Representation | A modular compiler infrastructure within LLVM providing extensible dialects for domain-specific transformations and multi-stage hardware/software lowering. |
| **TLM** | transaction-level model | A high-level abstraction for modeling digital systems where module communication is represented as abstract transactions rather than pin-level clock cycles. |
| **VCD** | value change dump | An ASCII-based industry standard waveform file format capturing signal value transitions during digital logic simulation. |
| **VLA** | vector-length-agnostic | A processor architecture or compiler property where software binaries dynamically adapt to any hardware vector register length without recompilation. |
: **EDA, Compilers and Intermediate Representations Glossary.** {#tbl-glossary-compilers tbl-colwidths="[15,30,55]"}

## Verification, Power and Standards {#sec-glossary-verification}

| **Acronym** | **Spelled-out form** | **Engineering definition** |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **BMC** | bounded model checking | A formal verification technique unrolling sequential circuit transitions up to a fixed depth $k$ and querying a SAT/SMT solver to prove or disprove properties. |
| **CDC** | clock-domain crossing | An interface where a signal generated in one clock domain is sampled in an asynchronous or unrelated clock domain, risking metastability. |
| **CEC** | combinational equivalence checking | A formal verification technique using SAT/BDD methods to prove that two combinational logic circuits produce identical Boolean outputs for all inputs. |
| **CEGAR** | counterexample-guided abstraction refinement | An iterative formal verification algorithm that starts with a coarse abstract model and progressively refines it using concrete counterexamples. |
| **FDIV** | floating-point division | A hardware arithmetic division unit, notably associated with the historic 1994 Pentium microprocessor verification defect. |
| **IEEE** | Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers | The professional engineering organization responsible for international standards including SystemVerilog (1800), SystemC (1666), and UPF (1801). |
| **PMP** | Physical Memory Protection | A RISC-V architectural standard providing hardware-enforced memory isolation and access permissions for physical memory regions. |
| **PRD** | product requirements document | A formal engineering document defining the functionality, performance targets, physical constraints, and delivery requirements for a hardware system. |
| **PST** | power state table | A tabular specification within IEEE 1801 UPF describing valid combinations of power domain voltage states and operating modes. |
| **RDC** | reset domain crossing | An asynchronous structural boundary where a signal originates in one reset domain and enters logic reset by an unrelated reset controller. |
| **RVWMO** | RISC-V Weak Memory Ordering | The canonical hardware memory consistency model for the RISC-V architecture defining legal ordering for multithreaded loads, stores, and fences. |
| **SDC** | Synopsys Design Constraints | The industry-standard Tcl-based timing and physical constraint format specifying clock frequencies, input/output delays, and multi-cycle false paths. |
| **SEC** | sequential equivalence checking | A formal verification method that mathematically proves two digital sequential circuits have identical input-output behavior over all cycles. |
| **SPEC** | Standard Performance Evaluation Corporation | A non-profit organization establishing standardized benchmark suites to measure computing system performance. |
| **SVA** | SystemVerilog Assertions | A declarative language extension within IEEE 1800 SystemVerilog used to specify temporal and Boolean properties for formal verification and dynamic simulation. |
| **UPF** | Unified Power Format | The standard declarative language (IEEE 1801) specifying power intent, power domains, isolation cells, level shifters, and power switches across physical synthesis. |
: **Verification, Power and Standards Glossary.** {#tbl-glossary-verification tbl-colwidths="[15,30,55]"}

## Bus Protocols and Interconnect Interfaces {#sec-glossary-interconnects}

| **Acronym** | **Spelled-out form** | **Engineering definition** |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **AMBA** | Arm Microcontroller Bus Architecture | An open-standard on-chip interconnect specification governing the connection and management of functional blocks in SoC designs. |
| **AXI** | Advanced eXtensible Interface | A high-performance, high-frequency, burst-based point-to-point interconnect protocol defined under the AMBA specification. |
| **AXI5** | Advanced eXtensible Interface 5 | The fifth-generation AMBA on-chip interconnect protocol standard providing high-performance point-to-point interface handshakes and atomic transactions. |
| **CXL** | Compute Express Link | An open industry-standard cache-coherent interconnect protocol running over PCIe physical layers for high-speed CPU-to-device and CPU-to-memory expansion. |
| **UCIe** | Universal Chiplet Interconnect Express | An open industry standard defining die-to-die physical, protocol, and software connectivity for 2.5D and 3D multi-chiplet integration. |
: **Bus Protocols and Interconnect Interfaces Glossary.** {#tbl-glossary-interconnects tbl-colwidths="[15,30,55]"}

## AI, Modeling and Design Automation {#sec-glossary-ai}

| **Acronym** | **Spelled-out form** | **Engineering definition** |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **AWC** | Autonomous Workflow Certified | A proposed artifact evaluation credential attesting to the computational reproducibility and explicit audit scope of an automated design workflow. |
| **BO** | Bayesian optimization | A sequential design strategy for global optimization of black-box objective functions using Gaussian process surrogate models and acquisition functions. |
| **CNN** | convolutional neural network | A class of deep neural networks using spatial convolution kernels, widely used in computer vision and structured tensor representations. |
| **DNN** | deep neural network | An artificial neural network with multiple hidden layers between input and output capable of learning hierarchical feature representations. |
| **DQN** | deep Q-network | A model-free reinforcement learning algorithm combining Q-learning with deep neural network function approximators. |
| **DSE** | design-space exploration | The systematic evaluation of architectural and microarchitectural parameters to identify Pareto-optimal trade-offs across power, performance, and area. |
| **ECE** | expected calibration error | A statistical metric measuring the difference between predicted model confidence probabilities and actual empirical accuracy. |
| **FP8** | 8-bit floating-point | A low-precision floating-point arithmetic format standardized for high-throughput deep learning training and inference. |
| **GNN** | graph neural network | A class of deep learning architectures operating directly on graph-structured data via message-passing between nodes and edges. |
| **HELM** | Holistic Evaluation of Language Models | A standardized benchmark framework that systematically evaluates foundation language models across diverse capabilities, risks, and behavioral metrics. |
| **INT4** | 4-bit integer | A quantized integer numeric representation using 4 bits per weight or activation to minimize memory bandwidth and footprint in deep learning accelerators. |
| **INT8** | 8-bit integer | An integer data format using 8 bits of precision commonly deployed in quantized neural network inference accelerators. |
| **KV** | key-value | A pair of tensors storing intermediate attention projections in transformer models, frequently cached across decoding steps. |
| **LLM** | large language model | A deep neural network trained on vast text or code corpora, capable of autoregressive token generation for natural language reasoning and code synthesis. |
| **MCTS** | Monte Carlo tree search | A heuristic search algorithm for decision processes combining tree traversal with Monte Carlo rollouts to evaluate candidate actions. |
| **MDP** | Markov decision process | A formal mathematical framework for modeling decision-making in discrete stochastic environments defined by states, actions, transition probabilities, and rewards. |
| **MoE** | mixture of experts | A neural network architecture routing individual input tokens to specialized expert sub-networks to scale parameter capacity with constant compute. |
| **OCI** | Open Container Initiative | An open governance structure standardizing container image formats and execution runtime specifications for software isolation. |
| **PPA** | power, performance, and area | The tripartite metric vector governing semiconductor optimization and architectural figure-of-merit evaluation. |
| **PPO** | proximal policy optimization | A model-free policy gradient reinforcement learning algorithm using clipped surrogate objectives to maintain stable policy updates. |
| **RL** | reinforcement learning | A machine learning paradigm where an autonomous agent learns to optimize a policy by taking actions in an environment to maximize cumulative reward signals. |
| **SLSA** | Supply Chain Levels for Software Artifacts | A security framework defining machine-readable, cryptographically signed metadata attestations for build provenance and supply chain integrity. |
: **AI, Modeling and Design Automation Glossary.** {#tbl-glossary-ai tbl-colwidths="[15,30,55]"}
